# 1 Enoch Chapter 103 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**1** I swear this to you, the righteous — by the majesty of his glory, by his power and greatness, by the sovereignty of his name. I swear: I know the mystery. I have read the heavenly tablets. I have seen the holy books. And I found it written there, inscribed — about their souls.

**2** Everything good, all joy, all glory — it is prepared for them. It is written down for the spirits of those who died in righteousness. You will be recompensed many times over for all your labors. Your portion will be immeasurably greater than the portion of those who are still alive.

**3** The spirits of those of you who died in righteousness will live — and they will celebrate. Their spirits will not perish. Their memory will stand before the face of the Great One through every generation, forever. So stop fearing the contempt of the wicked.

**4** Woe to you, sinners, when you die — if you die loaded down with your sins — and those who are just like you say about you: "What a blessed life the sinners had! They got to enjoy every single day.

**5** They died rich, prosperous — no tribulation, no murder in their lifetime. They died with honor. No judgment ever touched them while they were alive."

**6** Here is what you don't know: their souls will be driven down into Sheol, where they will suffer in terrible anguish.

**7** Their spirits will be thrown into darkness, into chains, into blazing fire — into a place of severe judgment. The great judgment will come for all the generations of the world. Woe to you — you will have no peace.

**8** Don't you dare use the righteous and good people still living as your evidence. Yes, we toiled in hard times. Yes, we experienced every kind of trouble. Yes, we were beaten down and had little left — few in number, crushed in spirit.

**9** Yes, we were destroyed. We found no one who would help us — not even a word of support. We were tortured. We were ground down. We had no expectation of living through to tomorrow.

**10** We were supposed to be the head — we became the tail. We worked and worked and got nothing from it. We became food for the wicked and the unrighteous. They crushed us under their yoke.

**11** Our enemies ruled over us and beat us. We bent our necks to those who hated us, and they showed us no mercy.

**12** We tried to get away from them — we wanted to escape, to finally rest — and we couldn't find anywhere to go, anywhere safe to run.

**13** We went to the rulers, crying, begging them to help us in our suffering. We raised our voices against those who were consuming us. They ignored us. They would not listen.

**14** Instead, they sided with the very people who were robbing us and destroying us and killing us off one by one. They covered up the oppression. They never lifted the yoke of those who scattered us and murdered us — and they covered up those murders too. They never remembered what our enemies had done with their hands against us.

**15** But I swear this to you, the righteous: in heaven, the angels are remembering you — speaking well of you before the glory of the Great One. Your names are written before the glory of the Great One.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Vv. 8–14 are the single most sociologically detailed passage in 1 Enoch — and arguably in all Second Temple literature. This is not apocalyptic abstraction. This is a community's testimony about real judicial corruption, real labor exploitation, real murder, and real institutional cover-up. The power of v. 15 depends entirely on how fully the horror of vv. 8–14 has been allowed to land. V. 15's counter: when human rulers looked away, heaven was watching and remembering.*
